title: Flag-day rehearsal on a synthetic keyring
description: End-to-end: a synthetic pgpkeys-like repo of throwaway GPG keys with certifications (incl. SHA-1 and an expired key), run port -> register --from -> verify-continuity -> drafts -> endorse -> approve -> check -> export -> sign a tag -> git verify-tag. Proves the runbook.
acceptance_criteria: Scripted rehearsal passes; every step's command is the one the docs will print.
notes:
Rehearsal: tests/migrate/rehearsal.sh (the runbook; docs/flag-day.md should print its non-harness lines) run by tests/migrate/test_rehearsal.py. Findings for omzm.6: (1) expired GPG key (D9): gpg refuses to sign with it; holder runs 'gpg --quick-set-expire <fpr> 1y' locally (never publish), then 'gpg --armor --detach-sign people/<h>.json'; verified at C gpg says EXPKEYSIG+VALIDSIG and migrate accepts it. (2) auth-subkey reuse: enable-ssh-support + keygrip in sshcontrol, 'gpg --export-ssh-key <email> > ~/.ssh/gpg-auth.pub', 'git vouch register --from <draft> --sign-with ~/.ssh/gpg-auth.pub' (draft already lists the key). (3) signing endorsement drafts: no git-vouch command does it; rehearsal uses 'ssh-keygen -Y sign -f ~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub -n git-vouch-endorse <draft>' then copies drafts+sigs in (QUESTION: add 'git vouch endorse --from DRAFT'?). (4) each holder runs 'git-vouch-migrate port' themselves (deterministic from public pgpkeys@C). (5) first merge: lena's person file, then anchors.json committed by the registry maintainer (anchors.json naming a handle with no person file fails check).
(6) review fixes: certifier must read each draft before signing (subjectName comes from the subject's own person file); runbook shows 'cat' then signs per file. Release verify-tag passes -c gpg.ssh.revocationFile explicitly so it works on a machine that never ran setup. Contributor-tier export proves bob's key verifies, so the maintainer-tier rejection is due to tier.
